t: Within 45 days after the close of each month, the Chief Financial Officer of the Department of Homeland Security shall submit to the Committees on Appropriations of the Senate and the House of Representatives a monthly budget and staffing report that includes total obligations, on-board versus funded full-time equivalent staffing levels, and the number of contract employees by office.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that a mandated report is a form of procedural consultation, but the report goes from a federal official to congressional committees, which are inside the federal government. No state, tribe, company, expert, or member of the public is consulted or given a role in any federal decision. The mention of contract employees is only a data item in the report, not an outside-party process.
fable.s: the Chief Financial Officer of the Department of Homeland Security shall submit to the Committees on Appropriations of the Senate and the House of Representatives a monthly budget and staffing report

opus.w: The section only requires a DHS official to send a monthly budget and staffing report to congressional committees, and Congress is inside the federal government. It provides no comment period, hearing, advisory body, outside consultation or right to sue. Reading the formal reporting requirement as participation would be wrong, because reports to Congress are an expressly listed trap.
opus.s: the Chief Financial Officer of the Department of Homeland Security shall submit to the Committees on Appropriations of the Senate and the House of Representatives a monthly budget and staffing report
opus.b: 1. **Tempting-but-wrong reading:** The section sets up a recurring formal process, a monthly budget and staffing report. That can look like structured participation in oversight. But the report goes from a DHS official (the Chief Financial Officer) to the House and Senate Appropriations Committees, and both are inside the federal government. No state, tribe, company, expert or member of the public is involved, so the section never crosses the federal boundary.

qwen_chat.w: The section requires a federal official (the Chief Financial Officer) to submit a report to Congressional committees. According to the definition, Congress and its committees are inside the federal government. Therefore, this is intra-governmental reporting, not participation with outside parties.
qwen_chat.s: the Chief Financial Officer of the Department of Homeland Security shall submit to the Committees on Appropriations of the Senate and the House of Representatives a monthly budget and staffing report
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the report is submitted to Congressional committees, it involves an external check or oversight, thus constituting participation. However, the definition explicitly states that "Congress, its committees and members... are all INSIDE the federal government." Therefore, reporting to Congress is intra-governmental communication, not participation with outside parties.
